BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.standard_title: Bureau of Indian Standards Act 2016 & Conformity Assessment Regulations
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.clause:
Section 13 — Grant and Renewal of License
Under Section 13 of the BIS Act 2016
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.content: , the Bureau of Indian Standards is the sole statutory authority empowered to grant, renew, suspend, or cancel a license to use the Standard Mark (ISI mark) or grant a Certificate of Conformity / Compulsory Registration. Third-party consulting platforms and software tools (such as ISense) are independent technical assistance providers and have no legal authority to issue licenses, certify products, or approve regulatory submissions.
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution — BIS Directorate

BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.standard_title: Bureau of Indian Standards Act 2016 & Conformity Assessment Regulations
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.clause:
Section 16 — Mandatory Quality Control Orders
The Central Government
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.content: , by order published in the Official Gazette, may direct that any goods, article, process, system or service of any scheduled industry shall conform to an Indian Standard and direct the use of the Standard Mark under a license or certificate of conformity. No person shall manufacture, import, distribute, sell, or expose for sale any goods covered under a mandatory Quality Control Order (QCO) without a valid license or registration issued by BIS.
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution — BIS Directorate

BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.standard_title: Bureau of Indian Standards Act 2016 & Conformity Assessment Regulations
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.clause:
Section 29 — Penalties for Unauthorized Use
Any person who makes unauthorized use of the Standard Mark or contravenes mandatory notification orders under Section 16 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term up to two years or with fine which shall not be less than two lakh rupees
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.content: , extending up to ten times the value of goods produced or sold.
BIS_Act_2016_Statutory_Framework.md.authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution — BIS Directorate

BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.standard_title: Statutory Application Fees, Marking Fees and Processing Timelines
BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.content:
(CRS / Scheme II) Statutory Fees
1. Application Filing Fee: ₹1,000 per application (non-refundable).
2. Processing Fee: ₹50,000 for primary product category (valid for 2 years registration). Additional series models attract ₹10,000 to ₹20,000 scrutiny fee per addition.
3. Laboratory Testing Charges: Incurred separately, payable directly to the recognized testing laboratory (LRS/NABL) depending on testing scope.
4. Renewal Fee: ₹50,000 for two-year renewal extension.
BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards Central Finance Directorate

BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.standard_title: Statutory Application Fees, Marking Fees and Processing Timelines
BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.content:
(Scheme I / ISI Mark Domestic)
1. Application Fee: ₹1,000 (non-refundable).
2. Factory Inspection Fee: ₹7,000 per man-day for inspecting officers plus actual travel and accommodation expenses.
3. Annual License Fee: ₹1,000 payable upon grant and each year of license tenure.
4. Marking Fee: Calculated based on production unit volume as defined in the Scheme of Testing and Inspection (STI), subject to a minimum statutory marking fee per annum.
BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards Central Finance Directorate

BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.standard_title: Statutory Application Fees, Marking Fees and Processing Timelines
BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.clause:
Schedule 2 — Processing Timelines and Service Standards
- CRS
BIS_Financial_Regulations_Fees_Timelines.content:
(Scheme II): 15 to 30 working days from date of submission of complete technical dossier with valid accredited test report issued within 90 days.
- Scheme I (Domestic ISI Mark): 60 to 90 working days, including preliminary inspection, sample verification, and counter-sample testing.
- Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS): 90 to 180 working days due to international travel, visa approvals, and customs clearance of verification samples.

IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.standard_title: Plugs and Socket-Outlets of Rated Voltage up to and Including 250 Volts and Rated Current up to and Including 16 Amperes
IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.clause:
Clause 1 — Scope
Applies to plugs and fixed or portable socket-outlets for AC only
IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.content: , with or without earthing contact, rated between 2.5A and 16A at voltages up to 250V, including smart plugs and Wi-Fi sockets.

IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.standard_title: Plugs and Socket-Outlets of Rated Voltage up to and Including 250 Volts and Rated Current up to and Including 16 Amperes
IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.clause:
Clause 9 — Dimensional Verification and Gauges
Plug pins shall have solid cylindrical construction
IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.content: (solid brass or nickel plated). Shuttered socket-outlets are mandatory for all domestic installations to prevent contact of children with live apertures. Gauge testing verifies insertion depth, pin diameter, and centre-to-centre pin spacing conforming to Sheet 1 (6A) and Sheet 2 (16A).

IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.standard_title: Plugs and Socket-Outlets of Rated Voltage up to and Including 250 Volts and Rated Current up to and Including 16 Amperes
IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.clause:
Clause 13.3 — Glow-Wire Thermal Resistance Test
Insulating components retaining current-carrying parts in position are subjected to a glow-wire loop heated to 750
IS_1293_2019_Plugs_and_Sockets.md.content: °C (or 850°C for unattended smart plugs) applied for 30 seconds. Flames or glowing must extinguish within 30 seconds of removing the glow-wire tip, and burning droplets must not ignite tissue paper placed below.

Applies to mains-powered or battery-powered information technology equipment

Minimum clearance across isolation barriers for reinforced insulation is 4.0 mm

(Hi-Pot Test)
Reinforced insulation between primary AC input circuits and accessible secondary DC circuits must withstand a high-voltage test potential of 3000V AC rms (or 4242V DC peak) for 60 seconds without breakdown or excessive leakage current.

External plastic enclosures housing primary components must have a minimum UL94 V-1 flammability rating

IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.standard_title: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes (Lithium Systems)
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.clause:
Clause 1 — Scope
Specifies requirements and tests for the safe operation of portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.content: (including power banks, mobile phone batteries, laptop batteries) containing non-acid electrolytes under intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse.
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) & BIS (LITD 10)

IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.standard_title: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes (Lithium Systems)
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.clause:
Clause 7.3.2 — External Short Circuit Test
Fully charged battery packs and cells shall be short-circuited by connecting the positive and negative terminals with an external resistance of 80
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.content: ± 20 mOhms at 55 ± 5°C. The short circuit condition is maintained until the case temperature drops back below peak by 20%. The cell or battery pack shall not explode, catch fire, or exceed 150°C during test duration.
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) & BIS (LITD 10)

IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.standard_title: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes (Lithium Systems)
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.content:
/ Drop Test
Each cell or battery is dropped three times from a height of 1.0 meter onto a smooth, horizontal concrete surface in each of the three mutually perpendicular axes. The test specimens shall exhibit no fire, explosion, or chemical electrolyte leakage.
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) & BIS (LITD 10)

IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.standard_title: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes (Lithium Systems)
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.clause:
Clause 7.3.5 — Thermal Abuse Test
The cell is placed in a gravity convection or circulating air oven heated at a rate of 5
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.content: °C/min to 130 ± 2°C and held at this temperature for 10 minutes. Cells shall not catch fire or explode.
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) & BIS (LITD 10)

IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.standard_title: Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes (Lithium Systems)
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.clause:
Clause 7.3.6 — Overcharging Test for Battery Packs
The battery pack is charged from discharged state with a charging current of 2.0 times rated capacity
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.content: (2C) up to maximum allowable voltage limits. Protection circuits must disconnect charging before catastrophic failure or thermal runaway occurs.
IS_16046_Part2_2018_Lithium_Batteries.md.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) & BIS (LITD 10)

IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.standard_title: Self-Ballasted LED-Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements

IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.standard_title: Self-Ballasted LED-Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.clause:
Clause 1 — Scope
This standard specifies the safety and interchangeability requirements
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.content: , together with the test methods and conditions required to show compliance of LED lamps with integrated means for controlling, intended for domestic and similar general lighting purposes. Applies to self-ballasted LED lamps having rated wattage up to 60W and rated voltage up to 250V AC.
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards — Electrotechnical Division (ETD 23)

IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.standard_title: Self-Ballasted LED-Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.clause:
Clause 5 — Marking Protocol
Lamps shall be clearly and durably marked with:
1. Mark of origin
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.content:
(manufacturer name or registered trademark).
2. Rated supply voltage or voltage range (Volts).
3. Rated wattage (Watts).
4. Rated frequency (Hertz).
5. Rated lamp current or luminous flux.
Marking legibility is verified by rubbing for 15 seconds with a cloth soaked in water, and for 15 seconds with a cloth soaked in petroleum spirit. After the test, the marking must remain legible.
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards — Electrotechnical Division (ETD 23)

IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.standard_title: Self-Ballasted LED-Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.clause:
Clause 8.0 — Insulation Resistance and Electric Strength
Insulation resistance between live parts and accessible metal parts shall not be less than 4.0 Megohms when tested at 500V DC applied for 1 minute under ambient damp heat conditioning.
Electric strength test: High-voltage insulation withstand of 1500V AC rms
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.content: (or 2120V DC) applied between live parts and accessible parts for 1 minute without dielectric breakdown or flashover.
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards — Electrotechnical Division (ETD 23)

IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.standard_title: Self-Ballasted LED-Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.content:
(Cap Torque Resistance)
The lamp cap shall remain firmly attached to the lamp body when subjected to a minimum mechanical torque:
- B22d and E27 caps: minimum 3.0 Newton-meters (Nm) retention torque.
- E14 caps: minimum 1.15 Newton-meters (Nm) retention torque.
Testing is carried out using a standardized cap torque test fixture without loosening or electrical disruption.
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards — Electrotechnical Division (ETD 23)

IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.standard_title: Self-Ballasted LED-Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.clause:
Clause 12 — Creepage Distance and Clearance
Clearance and creepage distances between live parts and accessible metallic surfaces shall conform to Table 1: minimum creepage distance is 3.0mm
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.content: , and minimum clearance distance is 2.5mm for rated voltage 250V.
IS_16102_Part1_2012_LED_Lamps.md.authority: Bureau of Indian Standards — Electrotechnical Division (ETD 23)

IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.standard_title: Test Procedure of Islanding Prevention Measures for Utility-Interconnected Photovoltaic Inverters
IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.content:
(RLC Tuning)
The test circuit shall couple the inverter under test to an AC power source and an adjustable resonant RLC load having a quality factor (Qf) of 1.0. Active power and reactive power must be balanced to zero flow from the utility grid prior to switch opening.
IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) & BIS Electrotechnical Division (ETD 28)

IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.standard_title: Test Procedure of Islanding Prevention Measures for Utility-Interconnected Photovoltaic Inverters
IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.clause:
Clause 4.3 — Islanding Trip Disconnect Time Threshold
The islanding condition is initiated by opening the utility isolation switch. The disconnect trip time
IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.content: (run-on time) shall not exceed 2.0 seconds under test power levels of 25%, 50%, 100%, and 125% of rated inverter output. Inverters exceeding 2.0 seconds disconnect time fail compliance.
IS_16169_2014_Islanding_Prevention.md.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) & BIS Electrotechnical Division (ETD 28)

IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.clause:
Clause 1 — Scope and Application
This Indian Standard covers the particular safety requirements for grid-connected and standalone power converters
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.content: (inverters) used in photovoltaic (PV) power systems. Applies to utility-interconnected inverters with DC input voltages up to 1500V DC and AC output up to 1000V AC.
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) & BIS Solar Energy Division (ETD 28)

IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.standard_title: Safety of Power Converters for Use in Photovoltaic Power Systems - Particular Requirements for Inverters
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.clause:
Clause 4 — Protection Against Electric Shock and Isolation
The inverter must maintain complete galvanic or functional isolation between hazardous DC array voltages and touchable enclosure parts. DC insulation resistance must exceed 1.0 Megohm measured at 1000V DC between the array input conductors
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) & BIS Solar Energy Division (ETD 28)

IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.standard_title: Safety of Power Converters for Use in Photovoltaic Power Systems - Particular Requirements for Inverters
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.clause:
Clause 5.1 — Automated Anti-Islanding Protection
Grid-connected photovoltaic inverters shall incorporate an automatic anti-islanding detection system. Upon disconnection from the utility grid or upon line voltage
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.content: /frequency drifting outside statutory limits, the inverter shall disconnect and cease to energize the utility line within a maximum time of 2.0 seconds.
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) & BIS Solar Energy Division (ETD 28)

IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.standard_title: Safety of Power Converters for Use in Photovoltaic Power Systems - Particular Requirements for Inverters
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.clause:
Clause 6.3 — Residual Current and Ground Fault Detection
Inverters shall incorporate continuous residual current monitoring
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.content: (RCMU). If an excessive residual fault current exceeding 300 mA (or 30 mA continuous touch leakage) is detected on the DC or AC circuit, the inverter must trip and isolate within 300 milliseconds.
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.authority: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) & BIS Solar Energy Division (ETD 28)

IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.standard_title: Safety of Power Converters for Use in Photovoltaic Power Systems - Particular Requirements for Inverters
IS_16221_Part2_2015_Solar_Inverters.md.clause:
Clause 8 — Temperature Limits and Fire Resistance
Enclosure materials must satisfy glow-wire and UL94 flammability requirements. All power semiconductor heat sinks and transformers must operate within specified thermal class limits under 50

Covers dedicated off-board equipment and AC

& Functional Interlock
The EVSE must communicate with the vehicle using a pulse-width modulated (PWM) pilot signal on the control pilot line. IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.standard_title: Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Safety & Performance Specification
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.clause:
Clause 1 — Scope
Applies to ceiling fans with AC induction motors or Brushless DC
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.content: (BLDC) motors, suitable for domestic and commercial installation, with sweeps between 600 mm and 1500 mm.

IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.standard_title: Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Safety & Performance Specification
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.clause:
Clause 11 — Mechanical Suspension and Shackle Safety
The suspension shackle
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.content: , down-rod, and safety pin assembly shall possess adequate mechanical strength. The suspension assembly must withstand an axial tensile load of not less than 1000 N applied for 1 minute without permanent deformation or shear. A secondary safety retention wire or safety split-pin is mandatory.

IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.standard_title: Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Safety & Performance Specification
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.clause:
Clause 14 — Air Delivery and Service Value
Air delivery is tested in an airtight test chamber with anemometer array:
- For 1200 mm sweep fans: Minimum air delivery is 210 cubic meters per minute
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.content:
(m³/min).
- Minimum Service Value (air delivery divided by input wattage) for BLDC energy-efficient ceiling fans must be not less than 5.0 m³/min/Watt to qualify under Star Rating benchmarks.

IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.standard_title: Electric Ceiling Type Fans and Regulators — Safety & Performance Specification
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.clause:
Clause 15 — Temperature Rise and Insulation Endurance
Motor winding temperature rise shall not exceed the permissible limit for the insulation class: Class A
IS_374_2019_Electric_Ceiling_Fans.md.content: (70°C), Class E (85°C), Class B (95°C), measured by the resistance change method after continuous operation until thermal equilibrium.

IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.standard_title: Protective Helmets for Two-Wheeler Riders — Specification

This standard covers the requirements regarding material
IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.content: , construction, workmanship, finish, and performance tests for protective helmets for everyday two-wheeler riders.

IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.clause:
Clause 7 — Visor Optical Performance and Clarity
Visors must deliver not less than 85
IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.content: % luminous transmittance for clear visors. Visors shall produce no optical distortion, double image, or astigmatism exceeding 0.12 diopters. Scratch resistance and mechanical impact shatter resistance must be verified without cracking into sharp fragments.
IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.authority: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) & BIS Transport Engineering Division (TED 18)

IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.standard_title: Protective Helmets for Two-Wheeler Riders — Specification
IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.clause:
Clause 9.1 — Impact Deceleration Attenuation Test
Helmets undergo conditioning under:
1. Ambient conditioning
IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.content:
(+25°C).
2. High temperature conditioning (+50°C).
3. Low temperature conditioning (-10°C).
4. Continuous water immersion.
Helmets are dropped onto flat steel and hemispherical steel anvils at an impact velocity of 7.5 m/s. The peak acceleration measured by a calibrated triaxial accelerometer fitted within the headform shall not exceed 300g (3000 m/s²), and the duration of acceleration exceeding 150g shall not exceed 5.0 milliseconds.

IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.standard_title: Protective Helmets for Two-Wheeler Riders — Specification
IS_4151_2020_Protective_Helmets.md.content:
(Chinstrap) Dynamic Strength
The retention system is tested on a retention test rig with an initial preload of 50N, followed by a dynamic drop impulse mass of 10.0 kg falling through a height of 750 mm. The maximum dynamic extension shall not exceed 25 mm, and residual permanent elongation shall not exceed 15 mm. The quick-release buckle must open under a release force between 10N and 30N after dynamic loading.
